newsitem.title: FRANCE: Maillot expects AOM talks to start in weeks.
newsitem.headline: Maillot expects AOM talks to start in weeks.

text.p: Jacques Maillot, chairman of travel agency Nouvelles Frontieres and its small airline Corsair, said he expected formal talks about the acquisition of airline AOM could start in a few weeks.
"AOM is totally different from Air Liberte," Maillot told Reuters by telephone.

"There is no question of a pending bankruptcy and while Air Liberte is private, AOM is owned by the state. There is no hurry," he said. Formal talks could start in a few weeks and the entire process would take several months, he added.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation (CDR) which is selling former assets of bank Credit Lyonnais.
"I have had several talks with CDR executives and we have started to exchange information," Maillot said.
"We have not talked about a price or anything. There is an old valuation by Warburgs and I have asked Banque Paribas to look at the company," he said.

"First there will be talks between Paribas and Warburgs, then we will start official talks with CDR. And because CDR is part of the state there have to be discussions with Bercy (Finance Ministry) and the Privatisation Commission," Maillot said.
Warburg had put a value of one billion francs on AOM but Maillot noted the study was a bit outdated as much had changed in the market since.

Maillot said he had no aim to merge AOM with his Corsair airline. "Nouvelles Frontieres is the main client, for 85 percent, of Corsair. AOM works with intermediaries and other travel agencies," he said.
"There can be cooperation on commercial issues, fuel supply or maintenance but that has to come from the companies themselves, it should not be imposed," he said.
"AOM would allow Nouvelles Frontieres to grow further," Maillot said.
AOM was formed in 1991 by the merger of Air Outre Mer and Minerve and was financed by the Altus Finance venture capital unit of Credit Lyonnais.
The stake in AOM was transferred to CDR as part of a state rescue deal of the distressed bank.
A spokesman for CDR said the consortium was in no hurry to sell AOM.
